name: mouth-to-stomach
prompt: Use case: scientific-educational. Finished Body School textbook illustration for children ages 11–13. White background, large bold navy sans-serif headings, pale blue rounded label panels, clean softly shaded anatomical art, friendly and non-gory, consistent with the existing lungs lesson. No watermark, no tiny text. PORTRAIT 4:5 composition. Exact title "From your mouth to your stomach". A simplified human side-profile head cutaway at top with visible mouth, teeth and tongue, then a vertical ESOPHAGUS leading downward behind the airway into a cutaway J-shaped stomach at lower right. The food tube must connect continuously from back of mouth to esophagus to stomach. Highlight FOOD route with orange arrows pointing downward; small food pieces visible only inside that route. The windpipe, if visible for orientation, must be faint and separate from highlighted esophagus. No arrows into the windpipe. Inside cutaway stomach, show pale golden liquid and softened food pieces with curved arrows illustrating mixing by muscular stomach wall. Labels with accurate leader lines: "Mouth", "Esophagus", "Stomach", "Digestive juices". No liver, intestines, blood vessels, or extra organs. Large enough stomach to clearly see mixing. All labels fully inside canvas.

name: small-intestine
prompt: Use case: scientific-educational. Finished Body School textbook illustration for children ages 11–13. White background, large bold navy sans-serif headings, pale blue rounded label panels, clean softly shaded anatomical art, friendly and non-gory, consistent with the existing lungs lesson. No watermark, no tiny text. SQUARE 1:1 composition. Exact title "The small intestine absorbs nutrients". At upper left, show a simplified pink coiled small intestine, label "Small intestine". A magnification connector leads to a large cutaway view of its INNER WALL occupying center and right: several slender finger-like VILLI project upward INTO the intestinal hollow space containing pale yellow liquid food. Label "Villi" with leader to the projections. One villus is cut open to reveal a fine red blood capillary loop INSIDE the villus, label "Blood vessel". Above the villi, small orange dots labeled "Nutrients". Two orange arrows move DOWNWARD from the nutrient dots in the liquid through the villus surface INTO its blood vessel. No arrows carrying whole food chunks into blood. The villi must grow continuously from the gut lining, not float separately. Warm pink tissues, red blood, gold nutrient dots; no blue blood. No hands or cartoon grabbing, no liver or large intestine.

name: large-intestine
prompt: Use case: scientific-educational. Finished Body School textbook illustration for children ages 11–13. White background, large bold navy sans-serif headings, pale blue rounded label panels, clean softly shaded anatomical art, friendly and non-gory, consistent with the existing lungs lesson. No watermark, no tiny text. SQUARE 1:1 composition. Exact title "The large intestine absorbs water". Main illustration: FRONT VIEW of the large intestine forming a frame around very faint pale small-intestine coils. Show cecum at viewer LEFT lower corner, ascending colon going UP viewer left, transverse colon across TOP toward viewer right, descending colon DOWN viewer right, sigmoid curving inward to central rectum and anus. Use orange route arrowheads INSIDE colon lumen in that correct direction, beginning at where small intestine enters cecum and ending downward through rectum to anus. Clear leader labels "Large intestine", "Rectum", "Anus". On lower right, small separate enlarged inset with a thin colon wall dividing liquid contents from a RED blood vessel. Blue water dots/arrows cross OUT of colon contents through the wall INTO the blood vessel, label "Water absorption". No waste arrows into blood and no urinary organs. Avoid stool close-ups. Rectum must be continuous with sigmoid colon; anus at end. Spacious legible labels.

name: liver-and-bile
prompt: Use case: scientific-educational. Finished Body School textbook illustration for children ages 11–13. White background, large bold navy sans-serif headings, pale blue rounded label panels, clean softly shaded anatomical art, friendly and non-gory, consistent with the existing lungs lesson. No watermark, no tiny text. WIDE 2:1 landscape composition. Exact title "The liver helps from the sidelines". Simplified anatomical schematic with large reddish-brown liver on viewer LEFT, small green gallbladder tucked beneath it, pink J-shaped stomach on viewer RIGHT receiving esophagus from above, and beginning of small intestine (duodenum) continuing from stomach outlet below. Show two CLEARLY DISTINCT continuous routes. ORANGE arrows for food follow esophagus -> stomach -> small intestine ONLY. GREEN arrows for bile follow liver and gallbladder -> bile duct -> small intestine. A thin green duct from liver joins gallbladder's short cystic duct, then the common bile duct ends in the inner wall of the duodenum AFTER stomach, never inside stomach. Food arrows must NEVER enter liver, gallbladder or bile duct. Labels "Liver", "Gallbladder", "Bile duct", "Stomach", "Small intestine". Bottom legend orange arrow "Food route" and green arrow "Bile route". Bottom short note "Food does not pass through the liver." Do not draw pancreas or unrelated organs, do not make gallbladder part of food tube. Large readable diagram with enough space for all labels.
